attempts.entry_title: CA1 movement and immobility place cells, their SWR reactivation and PFC modulation (Yu et al. 2017)
attempts.summary: In the five foraging rats of this dataset, the paper's CA1 findings mostly held up, while its prefrontal findings did not. Immobility-associated place cells fired at low speed at one reward well, and ripples carrying them were shorter, weaker, rarely shared with movement-associated cells and led by their spikes; their smaller spatial coverage did not reproduce. Fewer such cells passed selection than reported, likely because stored spike widths in two rats exceed the paper's cutoff. Only 33% of prefrontal units were modulated by ripple type, against 63%, and prefrontal firing at well entry could not be tested, as the data hold no entry times. Wells and the ripple threshold rest on the agent's own assumptions.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Yu, Kay, Liu, Grossrubatscher, Loback, Sosa, Chung, Karlsson, Larkin and Frank (2017) on CRCNS data set hc-13, which holds CA1 and prefrontal spikes, LFP and position of the five rats that performed the foraging task. It classifies CA1 place cells as immobility- or movement-associated, detects awake SWRs with the paper's noise-based threshold, and tests SWR content, CA1 pair coactivity and PFC SWR modulation. The W-track rats that the paper pools with the foraging rats are not in hc-13.

findings.statement: The data set holds no reward-well entry times (the infrared beam breaks the Methods use), no well positions and no rewarded-well contingencies; the task struct holds only the epoch type. Well visits must be inferred from position, and the claim that uses beam-break entries cannot be tested.
Only the task sessions (epochs 2, 4 and 6) are included; the rest sessions in the sleep box that the paper describes are not.

Stored spike widths of R1 and N2 run about 0.2 ms longer than in T1, S2 and Q1 (median 0.50 to 0.57 ms against 0.25 to 0.34 ms, CA1 and PFC alike), so the paper's < 0.4 ms pyramidal-cell rule removes every R1 and nearly every N2 CA1 unit. The Methods name two spike filters (600 to 6000 Hz or 300 to 6000 Hz); the data set does not say which animal used which, or how width should be compared across them.

No corpus callosum reference channel and no statement of the LFP's reference are included; the LFP is one channel per tetrode, presumably referenced at recording, so the ground-referenced LFP the Methods use for spectrograms cannot be rebuilt.
11 unit-days (in all five rats) have an empty area field in both cellinfo and tetinfo, though they have spikes, so it cannot be told whether they are CA1 or PFC units; they are left out.
Within a session, LFP start times differ across tetrodes by up to 45 ms in R1 and N2 (none in T1, S2, Q1); users must align tetrodes by their starttime field.
The data descriptor's summary says 'The CRCNS.org hc-7 data set contains recordings', for data set hc-13.

Question for the paper's authors. The SWR threshold (99.99th percentile of the mirrored noise distribution of 'envelope power') lies at about 0 to 0.8 z of the envelope amplitude here, giving about 2 SWRs per second of immobility, and below the mean for the squared envelope. Was the envelope amplitude or its square used, over which times was the histogram taken, and how many awake SWRs per day did the foraging rats give?

Question for the paper's authors. How were IAPs and MAPs selected in R1 and N2, whose stored spike widths mostly exceed 0.4 ms? Without the width rule there the MAP count (250) and the PFC selection (113) match the paper's 244 and 112.

Question for the paper's authors. Without beam-break times, which definition of a well visit (radius, minimum duration) reproduces the entries and exits of Figures 1 and 2 and the 6.4 to 6.6 s interval of Figure 1, supplement 1D?

entries.title: CA1 movement and immobility place cells, their SWR reactivation and PFC modulation (Yu et al. 2017)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Yu, Kay, Liu, Grossrubatscher, Loback, Sosa, Chung, Karlsson, Larkin and Frank (2017) on CRCNS data set hc-13, which holds CA1 and prefrontal spikes, LFP and position of the five rats that performed the foraging task. It classifies CA1 place cells as immobility- or movement-associated, detects awake SWRs with the paper's noise-based threshold, and tests SWR content, CA1 pair coactivity and PFC SWR modulation. The W-track rats that the paper pools with the foraging rats are not in hc-13.
